topicTitle: 10.3 Acidity of Water, Phenol, and Ethanol
answer: The phenoxide ion ($C_6H_5O^-$) is stabilised by delocalisation of the negative charge from oxygen into the $\pi$ system of the benzene ring (resonance). The ethoxide ion ($CH_3CH_2O^-$) has no such stabilisation. Hence phenol ($pK_a \approx 10$) is a much stronger acid than ethanol ($pK_a \approx 16$).
prompt: Why is phenol more acidic than ethanol? Explain in terms of conjugate base stability.

topicTitle: 10.3 Acidity of Water, Phenol, and Ethanol
answer: Ethanol < Water < Phenol. Ethanol is weakest (ethyl group +I effect destabilises ethoxide ion); water is intermediate; phenol is strongest (phenoxide ion stabilised by delocalisation into benzene ring). $pK_a$: Ethanol ≈ 16, Water ≈ 14, Phenol ≈ 10.
